captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a single, tapered aircraft wing section featuring a standard NACA aerodynamic profile. The wing is widest at its root chord and tapers down in both thickness and chord length towards the wing tip. The leading edge is smoothly rounded, while the trailing edge tapers to a sharp, thin point, with the entire span swept backward at a distinct angle.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric NACA 00xx series airfoil wing in OpenSCAD. The user should be able to configure key parameters including the chord length, the overall wing span/length, the maximum thickness as a percentage of the chord, the taper ratio of the wing tip relative to the root, and the sweep-back angle of the wing.
captions.factory: The design uses a mathematical function to calculate coordinate points along a NACA 00xx profile, creating a 2D polygon. This 2D profile is extruded into a thin 2.5D slice using linear_extrude. To generate the tapered, swept wing, a hull operation loft-connects the root 2.5D slice with a scaled and translated tip slice, while a custom transformation matrix (multmatrix) is applied to shear the geometry for the sweep-back angle.
